title: Onset of the transcontinental Amazon River
summary: Studies of offshore marine sediments date the start of the Amazon as a river crossing South America from the Andes to the Atlantic to the late Miocene. One study puts it between 9.4 and 9 million years ago, tied to Andean tectonism; an earlier study gave 11.8 to 11.3 million years ago, with the river reaching its present size in the late Pliocene.

uncertainty.note: Years are Ma with no 1950 offset. Hoorn et al. (2017): onset between 9.4 and 9 Ma; Figueiredo et al. (2009): between 11.8 and 11.3 Ma. The record spans both estimates; the onset age is still debated.

as_recorded.value: an onset of the transcontinental Amazon River between 9.4 and 9 Ma
initiated as a transcontinental river between 11.8 and 11.3 Ma ago (middle to late Miocene)

where.modern_name: Amazon Delta and mouth, northern Brazil (proxy pin; the evidence is from offshore wells and a borehole in the Foz do Amazonas Basin, and the river spans South America)
where.historical_name: Amazon drainage, northern South America; no polities

importance.justification: Birth of the world's largest river system, linked to Andean uplift.
